ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the attached figure is the same circuit diagram: on the left side is a 10 V voltage source; on the top, 5 kΩ, 4 kΩ, and 1 kΩ resistors are connected in series in sequence; the node between 5 kΩ and 4 kΩ is connected to the bottom common line through a 10 μF capacitor; the node between 4 kΩ and 1 kΩ is connected to the bottom common line through an ideal switch labeled t=0; the node after the rightmost 1 kΩ is connected to the bottom common line through a 1 mH inductor. The problem asks for the magnitude of the current flowing through the 4 kΩ resistor at t=0+ after the switch is closed. Reasoning: The switch has been open for a long time before t=0, so t=0− is the DC steady state. In the DC steady state, the capacitor is equivalent to an open circuit and the inductor is equivalent to a short circuit, so the three resistors 5 kΩ, 4 kΩ, and 1 kΩ are connected in series across the 10 V source. The steady-state current is I=10 V/(5+4+1) kΩ=1 mA. The voltage drop across the 5 kΩ resistor is 1 mA×5 kΩ=5 V, so the voltage at the node after 5 kΩ, that is, the upper node of the capacitor, is 10 V−5 V=5 V; therefore v_C(0−)=5 V. The capacitor voltage cannot change abruptly, so v_C(0+)=5 V. After the switch closes at t=0+, the right-end node of the 4 kΩ is shorted to the bottom common line by the ideal switch, namely 0 V; while the left-end node of the 4 kΩ is still held at 5 V by the capacitor. Therefore the magnitude of the voltage across the 4 kΩ is 5 V, and the magnitude of the current is |i|=5 V/4 kΩ=1.25 mA.
